speaker: Doctor
text:
Hello, I am Dr. Agent. You mentioned having a low-grade fever, itchy rash, and joint pain after taking antibiotics; can you tell me which specific antibiotic you were prescribed and how long you took it?

REQUEST TEST: Complete_Blood_Count, Erythrocyte_Sedimentation_Rate, Antinuclear_Antibody

speaker: Doctor
text: Those blood work results are normal, which is helpful. Did you experience any other symptoms like fatigue, sore throat, or swollen glands when the rash and joint pain started?

speaker: Patient
text: 8-year-old girl. The patient was brought to the emergency department because of a 2-day history of low-grade fever, itchy rash, and generalized joint pain. The rash initially started in the antecubital and popliteal fossae before spreading to the trunk and distal extremities. One week ago, she was diagnosed with acute sinusitis and started on amoxicillin. She has no history of adverse drug reactions, and her immunizations are up to date.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Amoxicillin-induced Drug Reaction with Eosinophilia and Systemic Symptoms (DRESS) syndrome. The combination of fever, generalized joint pain, and a specific morbilliform rash appearing 1-2 weeks after initiating amoxicillin is classic for this reaction; the normal CBC and ESR do not rule it out.
